speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, have you had any recent travel, eaten any suspicious foods, or taken new medications? Also, do you have a fever or see blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile.

REQUEST TEST: C. diff toxin assay.
REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this time.

I am confident in this diagnosis given your recent levofloxacin use and the onset of severe watery diarrhea. Would you like to discuss treatment options, or do you have any immediate concerns about your symptoms?
